headers.//: Hashed filenames — the content of any given URL here can never change, so holding it forever is both safe and the reason a repeat visit paints instantly. Freshness for these is handled by the filename, not by revalidation.

Photo filenames are the hash of their own contents, so a given URL can never mean a different image — immutable is literally true, and replacing a product's photo can never leave a device showing the old one.
The build stamp. Every running page compares this against the build it was served from, so a cached copy of it would defeat the entire check.
The build-time catalogue, used when /api/catalogue cannot be reached. Revalidated on every request so it is never served from a browser's disk cache after a deploy.
A write. Nothing about it is cacheable, and a cached 200 here would silently swallow a publish.
The admin panel itself is never served from a disk cache — the operator reloading after a deploy must get the new panel, not the one their browser kept.

rewrites.//: Only consulted when nothing matches on disk. A photo committed by the panel is served statically the moment a build includes it; until then this hands the request to a function that reads it out of the repository, so a freshly published product never shows a broken image while the build runs.
